Implementation is complete and the final build (the exact required command) succeeds.

## Summary

Implemented Phase 3 (Transcribe/Speech) per SPEC.md §5:

- **`modules/expo-speech/`** — new local Expo module mirroring `expo-health`'s structure: `ExpoSpeechModule.swift` wraps `SFSpeechRecognizer`/`SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` for authorization + streaming transcription (via `onPartialResult`/`onFinalResult`/`onError` events), plus matching TS types/wrapper.
- **`plugins/withSpeechSample.js`** — config plugin that registers `spec-assets/sample.wav` directly into the Xcode project's Resources build phase (via a relative path reference, no copying/modifying of `spec-assets/`), so it's bundled into the compiled app and loadable via `Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)`.
- **`app.json`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` and wired up the new plugin.
- **`screens/TranscribeScreen.tsx`** — wired to the native module: status line reflects auth state (refreshed on mount), `Request Access` triggers the OS permission prompt, `Transcribe Sample` streams live partial results and shows `Completed in N.N s` on completion, with native errors surfaced in the status line.

Verified end-to-end on the Simulator via idb: app launches without crashing, navigation works, the permission dialog shows the correct custom usage text, and status/button states update correctly through granted and error paths.

One caveat: actual speech-to-text output couldn't be verified in this sandbox — `SFSpeechRecognizer` fails there with `kAFAssistantErrorDomain` code 1101 (its local recognition daemon can't load a valid on-device model asset in this ephemeral Simulator, independent of the Simulator host being properly signed into iCloud/Siri-enabled). The failure path itself behaves correctly per spec: no crash, human-readable error text, button re-enables. This is very likely a limitation specific to this sandboxed environment rather than the implementation — worth confirming transcription end-to-end on your own machine's Simulator.
